2025
 The Honourable Smt Justice K. Sujana
 Tr.C.M.P.No.410 of 2024
Oral Order

:
This Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition is filed under Section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code,
1908 (for short 'CPC') seeking transfer of HMOP.No.76 of 2024 pending on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge Cum Additional Assistant Sessions Judge, at Siddipet, to the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Karimnagar.

2. Heard Sri Ponnam Mahesh Babu, learned counsel for petitioner/wife, and Sri B.Nagesh, learned counsel for respondent/husband.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the action of respondent in filing H.M.O.P. No.
76 of 2024, seeking divorce under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, at Siddipet,
is a deliberate attempt to harass and intimidate the petitioner.

He contended that the respondent and his family members had demanded dowry and subjected the petitioner to domestic violence immediately after marriage, forcing the petitioner to file a complaint, which was registered as FIR No. 17 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 506 of IPC, and Section 4 of the DP Act, before Karimnagar Women Police Station.

He asserted that the act SKS,J of respondent to file the H.M.O.P. at Siddipet,
despite the residence of petitioner being in Asif Nagar, Karimnagar, and the pending criminal case,
is a clear attempt to cause hardship and emotional trauma to the petitioner.
He averred that attending Court proceedings at Siddipet would require petitioner traveling alone, which would be unsafe and cause significant hardship to her.

He pointed out that there are already pending cases in Karimnagar, including a DVC case and an HMOP under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955,
for restitution of conjugal rights.
Therefore, he prayed this Court to allow this petition, transferring HMOP.No.76 of 2024 to the Court of Senior Civil Judge, Karimnagar.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent submitted that the respondent filed HMOP.No.76 of 2024 in the month of February 2024 and subsequent to filing of the said HMOP.,
the petitioner filed DVC case and restitution of conjugal rights case against the respondent.
He contended that the respondent is suffering with health issues, therefore, prayed this Court to dismiss the petition.
5. Having regard to the rival submissions made and on going through the material placed on record

,
it is noted that petitioner filed three cases against the respondent in Karimnagar and the SKS,J respondent is already attending the proceedings in the said cases.
Both parties filed different petitions under Section 9 and 31 of the Act, that being so, there is absolute requirement for the said cases to be decided by same Court.

However, considering the plea raised by the learned counsel for respondent with regard to health concern of respondent,
the attendance of respondent in HMOP.No.76 of 2024 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge,
Karimnagar, is dispensed with, unless his presence is specifically required during the course of trial,
subject to the condition of respondent being represented by his counsel on every date of hearing.
There shall be no order as to costs.

 The Honourable Smt Justice K. Sujana
 Tr.C.M.P.No.410 of 2024

:
This Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition is filed under Section 24 of the Civil Procedure Code,
1908 (for short 'CPC') seeking transfer of HMOP.No.76 of 2024 pending on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge Cum Additional Assistant Sessions Judge, at Siddipet, to the file of the Senior Civil Judge, Karimnagar.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the action of respondent in filing H.M.O.P. No.
76 of 2024, seeking divorce under Section 13(1)(ia)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, at Siddipet,
is a deliberate attempt to harass and intimidate the petitioner.
He contended that the respondent and his family members had demanded dowry and subjected the petitioner to domestic violence immediately after marriage, forcing the petitioner to file a complaint, which was registered as FIR No. 17 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 506 of IPC, and Section 4 of the DP Act, before Karimnagar Women Police Station.
He contended that the respondent is suffering with health issues, therefore, prayed this Court to dismiss the petition.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Both parties filed different petitions under Section 9 and 31 of the Act, that being so, there is absolute requirement for the said cases to be decided by same Court.
It is pertinent to note that in respect of transfer of proceedings of a matrimonial dispute, the convenience of the wife is to be preferred over the convenience of husband, as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Rajani Kishor Paradeshi Vs. Kishore Babulal Paradeshi 1 and Sumita singh Vs. Kumar Sanjay and another 2.
Hence, this Court is of the opinion that sufficient grounds are made out on facts and in law to accept the plea of the petitioner/wife to transfer HMOP.No.76 of 2024 from the Court of the Principal Senior Civil Judge Cum Additional Assistant Sessions Judge, at Siddipet, to the Court of the Senior Civil Judge, Karimnagar.
opennyai_summary.decision:
7. Accordingly, the Transfer Civil Miscellaneous Petition is allowed.
HMOP.No.76 of 2024 stands transferred from the Court of the Principal Senior Civil Judge Cum Additional Assistant Sessions Judge, at Siddipet, to the Court of the Senior Civil Judge, Karimnagar.
The Court concerned is hereby directed to transmit the entire case file relating to HMOP.No.76 of 2024 after duly (2005) 12 SCC 237 AIR 2002 SC 396 SKS,J indexed, within a period of one (1) month from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, under the due intimation of the same to the other side.
However, considering the plea raised by the learned counsel for respondent with regard to health concern of respondent,
the attendance of respondent in HMOP.No.76 of 2024 on the file of the Senior Civil Judge,
Karimnagar, is dispensed with, unless his presence is specifically required during the course of trial,
subject to the condition of respondent being represented by his counsel on every date of hearing.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
